answer_1.quote: We propose a zero-shot generation method to generate a task-oriented utterance from an intent description
answer_1.outputs: task-oriented utterances conditioned on intent descriptions

answer_2.quote: We use several quality metrics to assess the generated data: (i) we use multiple fluency and diversity metrics, (ii) we account for the performance of the classifiers trained on the generated data.

answer_4.quote: We perform two crowdsourcing studies to evaluate the quality of generated utterances, which aim at the evaluation of semantic correctness and fluency.
answer_4.guideline: First, we asked crowd workers to evaluate semantic correctness. We gave crowd workers an utterance and asked them to assign one of the four provided intent descriptions; a correct option was among them... Second, we asked crowd workers to evaluate the fluency of generated utterances. Crowd workers were provided with an utterance and were asked to score it on a Likert-type scale from 1 to 5, where (5) means that the utterance sounds natural, (3) means that the utterance contains some errors, (1) means that it is hard or even impossible to understand the utterance.
